# Detail Bug Report

https://app.detail.dev/org_d38a878f-9df9-4c4b-a96a-f5180b860085/bugs/bug_262442e7-36cf-459d-b754-3becfa715e23

Introduced in [#99](https://github.com/elviskahoro/buridan-ui/pull/99) by @LineIndent on Jul 4, 2026

# Summary
- **Context**: `field_demo()` is the live "General" example on the Field component docs page (`docs/components/field.md` renders it via `--DEMO(field_demo)--`). It is a checkout-style form whose Month/Year expiry selects are built from `{"label": ..., "value": ...}` item dicts passed straight through to Base UI's `Select.Root` by `components/ui/select.py`.
- **Bug**: The Month and Year selects are given `default_value="MM"` / `default_value="YYYY"`, but those strings are the placeholder *labels*, not item *values* — the placeholder items are `{"label": "MM", "value": ""}` and `{"label": "YYYY", "value": ""}`. The selects therefore start in an internal state of "a real option is selected" while that value corresponds to no registered item.
- **Actual vs. expected**: The trigger coincidentally still displays "MM"/"YYYY" via Base UI's raw-value stringify fallback, but `data-placeholder` is never set (so the muted placeholder styling `data-placeholder:text-muted-foreground` does not apply) and the select's visually hidden form input (a regular `<input>` hidden via CSS, not `type="hidden"`) is initialized to the fake values `"MM"`/`"YYYY"` as if the user had chosen an option; the correct behavior (verified by an SSR reproduction with the pinned `@base-ui/react@1.6.0`) is achieved with `default_value=""`, which renders the identical "MM"/"YYYY" text *with* `data-placeholder` set and an empty hidden input value.
- **Impact**: The rendered docs demo starts with a bogus form state — the select's visually hidden form input is initialized to `value="MM"`/`value="YYYY"` instead of an unset placeholder (as visible to anything wiring `on_value_change` or reading the input), and the trigger text is styled as a real selection rather than a muted placeholder; anyone copying the demo inherits the same wrong pattern.

# Code with Bug
`app/www/library/examples/field_general.py` (also duplicated in `assets/docs/components/field.md`):

```python
months = [
    {"label": "MM", "value": ""},   # placeholder item's value is "", not "MM"
    {"label": "01", "value": "01"},
    ...
]

...

select.root(
    select.trigger(
        select.value(),
        select.icon(),
        id="checkout-exp-month",
    ),
    ...
    items=months,
    default_value="MM",   # <-- BUG 🔴 label used as value; matches no item (placeholder value is "")
),
```

```python
years = [
    {"label": "YYYY", "value": ""},   # placeholder item's value is "", not "YYYY"
    ...
]

select.root(
    select.trigger(
        select.value(),
        select.icon(),
        id="checkout-exp-year",
    ),
    ...
    items=years,
    default_value="YYYY",   # <-- BUG 🔴 label used as value; matches no item (placeholder value is "")
),
```

# Explanation
Base UI `Select.Root` matches `default_value` against item **values**. With `default_value="MM"`/`"YYYY"` (not present in the items), Base UI treats the select as having a non-empty selected value (so it does not set `data-placeholder`) while also failing to match any registered item (so no item is actually selected). It still renders "MM"/"YYYY" because it falls back to stringifying the raw value when no matching item exists, masking the bug visually.

## Codebase Inconsistency
Other select examples consistently set `default_value` to an actual item value (e.g. `app/www/library/examples/select_groups.py`, `app/www/library/examples/select_align_items.py`, and all examples in `assets/docs/components/select.md`), unlike this Field demo which uses placeholder labels.

# Recommended Fix
Change the defaults to the placeholder items’ actual values in both copies so the demo stays in sync:

```python
items=months,
default_value="",   # value of the {"label": "MM", "value": ""} placeholder item
```

```python
items=years,
default_value="",   # value of the {"label": "YYYY", "value": ""} placeholder item
```

# History
This bug was introduced in commit 755f3ed ("v0.9.1 release (#99)") when the Month/Year selects were added and `default_value="MM"` / `"YYYY"` was set alongside placeholder items whose values are `""`.

# Detail Bug Report

https://app.detail.dev/org_d38a878f-9df9-4c4b-a96a-f5180b860085/bugs/bug_c27b0933-ddf7-4013-ac56-64803fa3fb8b

Introduced in [#35](https://github.com/elviskahoro/buridan-ui/pull/35) by @LineIndent on May 24, 2025

# Summary
- **Context**: `app/www/library/getting_started/clientstate_components.py` is a "getting started" example library for `ClientStateVar` (path: `app/www/library/getting_started/`). The sibling function `form_state_pattern_example` is wired as a live demo via the `--demo(form_state_pattern_example)--` token in `docs/resources/client_state_var.md:56`, confirming the library's role as copy-pasteable, runnable example code rendered through `app/www/parser.py`.
- **Bug**: `conditional_rendering_pattern_example` builds its conditional branches with `rx.div(...)`, but `rx.div` does not exist in the installed reflex (`reflex==0.9.6`, per `uv.lock:714-715`), so the function raises `AttributeError: No reflex attribute div` every time it is *called*.
- **Actual vs. expected**: Expected — a working show/hide demo of a `ClientStateVar`-backed boolean; actual — an `AttributeError` at component-build time whenever the function is invoked.
- **Impact**: No committed doc page or test currently *calls* this function, so the crash is not production-visible today. A developer calling/copy-pasting this getting-started snippet (or wiring a future `--demo(conditional_rendering_pattern_example)--`) will hit `AttributeError: No reflex attribute div` (rendered as a localized red "Error in demo: ..." panel when invoked via the demo parser).

# Code with Bug
`app/www/library/getting_started/clientstate_components.py`

```python
def conditional_rendering_pattern_example():
    show_details = ClientStateVar.create("show_details", False)

    return rx.box(
        rx.button(
            "Toggle Details", on_click=show_details.set_value(~show_details.value)
        ),
        rx.cond(
            show_details.value,
            rx.div("Detailed information here..."),   # <-- BUG 🔴 rx.div is not a reflex attribute (AttributeError)
            rx.div("Click to show details"),         # <-- BUG 🔴 rx.div is not a reflex attribute (AttributeError)
        ),
    )
```

# Explanation
- The repository pins `reflex==0.9.6`, where `rx.div` is not defined (valid primitives used elsewhere include `rx.box`, `rx.fragment`, or `rx.el.div`).
- When `conditional_rendering_pattern_example()` is invoked, component construction hits `rx.div(...)` and raises `AttributeError: No reflex attribute div`, breaking the example.
- If wired through `app/www/parser.py` via a `--demo(...)--` token, the parser calls `obj()` to build the component and catches the exception, rendering a red "Error in demo: No reflex attribute div" message instead of the demo.

## Codebase Inconsistency
- The rest of `clientstate_components.py` (and the broader codebase) uses `rx.box`/`rx.fragment`/`rx.el.div` for containers; `rx.div` appears only in this one function, indicating an API typo rather than an intended pattern.

# Recommended Fix
Replace the two `rx.div(...)` calls with a valid Reflex container primitive (matching the sibling example’s convention):

```python
        rx.cond(
            show_details.value,
            rx.box("Detailed information here..."),   # <-- FIX 🟢 use rx.box (valid)
            rx.box("Click to show details"),          # <-- FIX 🟢 use rx.box (valid)
        )
```

# History
This bug was introduced in commit 6222734. That commit ("client state var documentation (#35)", 2025-05-24) created the original snippet using `rx.div(...)` in both branches of `rx.cond`; subsequent renames/moves did not change the buggy lines.
